content.thinking:
The bug is in `recomputeUsage`: it counts all members instead of only active ones.

Removed members never decrement `seatsUsed`. The usage listener only increments on join, not on removal. Pending invitations may also be excluded from the cached seat count.

The seat count must drop immediately when a member is removed, and the periodic recount must only include active members. Otherwise a workspace cannot downgrade to a smaller plan after removing users.

Revoking a pending invitation does not free its seat. Replacing an invitation with a fresh one also fails to release the seat. Only active, unaccepted invitations should hold seats. A fully occupied workspace must still reject new invites.

Found a bug in `recomputeUsage` in `usage-repository.ts`. It counts all members without filtering to active or non-archived ones.

`registerUsageListeners` increments seats on `member.joined` but never decrements them on `member.removed`, so seats never free up. Invitation seat usage may also be missing from billing calculations.

`countPendingInvitations` does not filter out revoked invitations. Revoked invites still count as pending seats, so seat usage never drops when an invitation is revoked.

`listPendingInvitations` already filters out revoked invitations correctly. The fix for `countPendingInvitations` is simply adding `isNull(invitations.revokedAt)`. Expired invitations are not mentioned in the bug, so they will be left unchanged.

The periodic recount should only count active members, not pending invitations. Pending seats are tracked separately at invite time via `countPendingInvitations` and `countActiveMembers`. The billing page reads from the usage cache rather than a live count.
A plan-limits test likely defines the expected behavior.

The plan-limits test expects a free tenant with four members to report four used units.

Only active, non-archived members should count toward seat usage. The growth tenant test does not constrain whether pending invitations are included in the cache.

Pending invitations are excluded from the cached seat count and tracked separately at invite time. Removing a member frees their seat immediately. Revoking a pending invitation does not return its seat, which causes the bug where a fully occupied workspace cannot accept new invites after revoking one.

The bug is in `countPendingInvitations`, which fails to exclude revoked invitations. Re-sending an invitation replaces the old one, but the revoked seat remains counted. This blocks new invites in a full workspace. After the fix, revoked invitations no longer count toward seat usage.

The fix is to add `isNull(invitations.revokedAt)` to `countPendingInvitations`. Expired invitations that are not revoked will still hold seats, matching the behavior of `listPendingInvitations`. I also need to verify whether `recomputeUsage` should filter archived members and require an active status.

The member repository already defines a `liveMemberPredicate` that excludes archived members. `countActiveMembers` applies both the active status filter and this predicate. Since `archiveMember` sets both `status` to "suspended" and `archivedAt`, filtering by active status alone should correctly exclude suspended and archived members from seat counts.

The recount currently counts all members including archived ones. The soft-delete module warns against raw `isNull` checks on `archivedAt`, but usage-repository already uses `isNull` for projects and issues. I need to decide whether to switch to `shouldFilterArchived` or keep the existing pattern.

I will filter members by both active status and archivedAt, matching countActiveMembers. The usage-repository does not need to use shouldFilterArchived.

I will use `eq(status, "active")` alongside `isNull(archivedAt)` to exclude suspended members from seat counts. I also need to subscribe to `member.removed` events to decrement `seatsUsed` immediately when a member leaves. I am considering whether the usage cache should also track invitation changes, since the billing page reads `seatsUsed`.

The billing page reads from the usage cache, so removing a member must immediately decrement `seatsUsed` there. Revoking an invitation is handled by the invite service using live counts, not the cached value. If tests route through the action layer instead of the service, the cache may never include pending invitations at all, which would prevent revocation from affecting seat usage.

I also need to check whether sending an invitation should immediately increment the seat cache for the billing page.
A usage-service comment indicates that every event changing a counted resource nudges the cache.
